rubric: DATABASES / INDEXES, CTES, WINDOWS AND VIEWS / CHAPTER 15

slides.title: Aggregate without collapsing
slides.main: A window function calculates over a set of rows but doesn't collapse them.

captions: GROUP BY turns a group's rows into one: details lost
We want every row with the group total beside it
A window function calculates over a window but returns a result for every row

slides.title: OVER
slides.main: OVER (…) marks a window; empty OVER () means all rows.

captions: SUM(total) OVER () — the sum over all rows, repeated in each
Row share: total / SUM(total) OVER ()
Inside OVER: PARTITION BY, ORDER BY and a frame

lines: SELECT m, total, SUM(total) OVER () AS s
SELECT m, ROUND(100.0 * total / SUM(total) OVER ())

slides.title: PARTITION BY
slides.main: PARTITION BY splits rows into windows like GROUP BY, but rows stay.

captions: PARTITION BY cust splits rows into windows; windows don't see each other
SUM(total) OVER (PARTITION BY cust) — customer total beside each order
Order's share of the customer's sum: total / customer total

slides.title: Running total
slides.main: SUM(x) OVER (ORDER BY …) — a running total.

captions: ORDER BY in a window: each row sees the previous rows and itself
SUM(total) OVER (ORDER BY m): 100, 250, 370, 550
Without ORDER BY the window is the whole table, and the total is the same in every row

frames.text:
row sees itself
and the past

lines: SELECT m, total, SUM(total) OVER (ORDER BY m) AS run
SELECT m, total, SUM(total) OVER () AS s

captions: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY …) assigns 1, 2, 3, … with no repeats
Among equal values the order is arbitrary — add a unique key
With PARTITION BY the numbering restarts in each group

lines: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC, name)
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cust ORDER BY created)

slides.title: RANK and DENSE_RANK
slides.main: RANK leaves gaps after a tie, DENSE_RANK doesn't.

captions: ROW_NUMBER: 1, 2, 3, 4 — everyone gets a different number
RANK: a tie shares a place, the next is skipped — 1, 2, 2, 4
DENSE_RANK: no gaps — 1, 2, 2, 3

slides.title: Top-N per group
slides.main: ROW_NUMBER in a CTE + WHERE rn <= N — top in each group.

captions: Number products by price within a category: ROW_NUMBER … PARTITION BY category
No window function in WHERE: take numbers up to two in the outer query
LIMIT would cap the whole result, not each category

lines: PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC) AS rn

slides.title: LAG and LEAD
slides.main: LAG takes the previous row's value, LEAD the next one's.

captions: LAG(total) — the previous row's value; NULL for the first
total − LAG(total): growth over the previous month
LEAD(total) — the next row's value

slides.title: FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE
slides.main: FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE take the window's first and last row value.

captions: FIRST_VALUE(total) — the first row's value: 100 in every row
LAST_VALUE by default gives the current row's value: the frame ends there
Extend the frame to the window's end for the real last value

slides.title: Window frame
slides.main: ROWS BETWEEN … AND … sets which rows each row sees.

captions: ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW — current and two previous
AVG over such a frame — a three-month moving average
Default frame with ORDER BY: window start to current row — a running total

lines: ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)

slides.title: NTILE and shares
slides.main: NTILE(n) splits rows into n equal groups; share = value / SUM() OVER ().

captions: NTILE(2) splits the ordered rows into two equal halves
NTILE(4) — quartiles: the top quarter of customers by amount
A row's share of the total: value / SUM(value) OVER ()

slides.title: Order of execution
slides.main: Windows run after WHERE, GROUP BY and HAVING, before ORDER BY.

captions: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → windows → SELECT → ORDER BY → LIMIT
A window sees only rows that passed WHERE — the filter changes its result
A condition on a window function's value — only in an outer query

frames.text: the sum counts only paid orders
